source: MAFF — សារៈប្រយោជន៍នៃដំណាំស្រូវ (Value of the Rice Crop) slide deck, presenter contact temseng@yahoo.com, p.12
text: Rice straw or stalk material can be bundled into large decorative sunburst/fan-shaped ornaments by radially arranging many short cut sticks of straw around a central point and gluing them in place (photographed being hand-assembled with a glue gun at what appears to be a community craft-making event or training). This is an example of a low-cost, community-level handicraft product made from a rice byproduct (straw) for decorative sale.

source: MAFF — សារៈប្រយោជន៍នៃដំណាំស្រូវ (Value of the Rice Crop) slide deck, presenter contact temseng@yahoo.com, p.14
text: Compressed rice straw/husk fiber can be molded into rigid, cardboard-like decorative and household items for the home décor and gift market. Examples shown include: tapered vases and plant/pen holders of varying heights, square planter or storage boxes, decorative wall discs made of interlocking rings of the material, a picture-frame-style craft clock, decorative trays, and straw-fiber flower arrangements, wreaths, and gift-wrapped ornamental plant pots finished with ribbon accents. This illustrates rice straw/husk as a raw material for an eco-friendly décor and handicraft product line, adding value to a crop residue that would otherwise be burned or left in the field.

source: MAFF — សារៈប្រយោជន៍នៃដំណាំស្រូវ (Value of the Rice Crop) slide deck, presenter contact temseng@yahoo.com, p.15
text: Rice straw fiber can be processed into handmade paper, visibly textured with straw fibers, which is then formed into products such as gift bags with rope handles (some decorated with small paper flower appliques). These appear to be small-scale artisanal/craft products, illustrating another value-added use of rice straw beyond animal feed, mulch, or fuel.

source: MAFF — សារៈប្រយោជន៍នៃដំណាំស្រូវ (Value of the Rice Crop) slide deck, presenter contact temseng@yahoo.com, p.16
text: Rice-straw handmade paper can also be mounted onto wooden or bamboo folding-fan ribs and hand-painted with decorative floral and cartoon-style designs to produce painted folding hand fans, sold as souvenir or craft-fair items. Together with the straw-fiber gift bags and molded décor items, this shows rice straw supporting a small artisanal handicraft and light-manufacturing value chain, likely suited to community groups, women's cooperatives, or youth training programs as a source of supplementary income from a rice by-product.
